title: Accepted Bottom Water-Thermal Substep Carrier Contract Freeze

invariants.assessment: The contract reuses the single F-KT/canonical runtime path and forbids a second energy-specific kernel.
No kernel I/O, parsing, path or file-format responsibility is introduced.
Thermal carrier scratch, accepted result metadata, immutable energy parameters, external forcing/coupler data and physical continuation state remain distinct categories.
The sample sequence is explicitly excluded from persistent column state; only physical temperature needed for continuation remains state.
The proposed sample carrier belongs to transaction attempt context owned by the worker/backend and is rollback scratch.
The future implementation is bounded worker scratch with sparse requested-column publication rather than an object-heavy permanent array per column.
Existing attempt-context checkpoint/restore selects full/half/retry samples transactionally; rejected routes and failed outer candidates publish nothing.
No extra physical solve is allowed to reconstruct discarded thermal history; recomputation and warm starts remain governed by existing committed-state semantics.
Every sample carries generic t0,t1; no day, month, year or midnight semantics are introduced.
Carrier and publication semantics are independent of coupling-window duration.
The design preserves accepted transfer provenance and rollback needed by coupled execution without embedding an application-specific coupler in SWAP.
No SWAP-MODFLOW head or flux equality contract is changed; later energy coupling must use the same conservative interface transfer.
The carrier consumes but never rebooks authoritative bottom water transfer; water mass conservation cannot be relaxed by energy accounting.
Interface sensitivity ownership and production remain unchanged.
The contract forbids additional Richards or thermal solves solely for energy history reconstruction.
Optional sparse result publication and worker-local scratch are compatible with large MultiSWAP batches without one heavy carrier object per logical column.
The carrier knows only a signed SWAP bottom transfer and no MODFLOW cell or tile fraction.
Deep-vadose mapping remains outside SWAP; thermal transport through a transfer zone is explicitly a separate component contract.
No stored water transition or component transfer is changed; later energy composition must accompany the same mass-conserving transition.
Public semantics are accepted-route transfer samples, not Richards or HeadCalc arrays. Alternative soil-water solvers may produce the same carrier contract with different internal sampling.
The design reuses current hydraulic and restricted thermal trial physics and does not import legacy global variables as architecture.
The contract requires typed physical/thermal state information and forbids dependence on HeadCalc internals.
Thermal activation and donor provenance are physical configuration/data; full/half/retry selection remains numerical policy and is not reinterpreted as physics.
Carrier cost is bounded by accepted-route sample count and numerical max_committed_substeps; missing thermal provenance is diagnostic rather than an unbounded retry trigger in this contract.
Reference execution remains the qualification baseline and no reference mode is removed or bypassed.
The next implementation gate requires explicit completeness/failure diagnostics and sample-route provenance.
Thermal carrier scratch and accepted records are required only for feature-active/requested columns.
MODFLOW, tile fractions, deep-vadose mapping and external donor ownership remain runtime/coupler/component responsibilities.
No .swp, file, calendar, midnight, direct-MODFLOW or fixed-window assumption is introduced.
This audit explicitly assesses the proposed carrier design against every architecture invariant before production implementation.

semantic_attacks.attack: full trial thermal sample survives when two-half route is selected
semantic_attacks.required_defense: attempt-context restore removes full-route sample before half-route execution and selected half context is restored on acceptance

semantic_attacks.attack: first-half donor temperature lost after half2 overwrites state
semantic_attacks.required_defense: sample is appended to attempt context before half2 and therefore survives in half-route scratch without retaining a full physical state clone
checkpoint context restore removes all samples from rejected attempt

semantic_attacks.attack: outer interval fails after prior internal accepted transaction
semantic_attacks.required_defense: candidate-scoped carrier remains nonpublic and is discarded with failed outer candidate

semantic_attacks.attack: incoming groundwater silently uses SWAP bottom temperature
semantic_attacks.required_defense: external donor classification is incomplete unless explicit external thermal provenance is supplied

semantic_attacks.attack: energy path duplicates bottom water mass ledger
semantic_attacks.required_defense: signed amount is referenced as authoritative transfer metadata and never becomes independent committed water state

semantic_attacks.attack: terminal temperature shortcut used for multi-sample interval
semantic_attacks.required_defense: ordered sample endpoints are preserved and no temporal quadrature is selected by EB-I12

semantic_attacks.attack: feature adds memory to every MultiSWAP column
semantic_attacks.required_defense: worker-local bounded scratch and sparse result request only

semantic_attacks.attack: lost provenance is reconstructed with extra physical runs
semantic_attacks.required_defense: contract explicitly forbids extra Richards or thermal solve for reconstruction

semantic_attacks.attack: energy bookkeeping contaminates physical restart state
semantic_attacks.required_defense: carrier sequence is temporary scratch/result metadata and excluded from persistent continuation state

hard_nonclaims: correction of restricted soil-temperature governing equation
